records.change: Omits "Jesus" and "settle"; prayer becomes promise
records.note: "Jesus" and "settle" are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or most early witnesses; Weymouth follows the latter. The critical text also has the verbs as future ("will"), as a promise.

records.change: Omits "Jesus" and "Amen"
records.note: "Jesus" and the "Amen" are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or most early witnesses; Weymouth follows the latter. The meaning is unchanged.

records.change: Omits "for ever" from the reserved darkness
records.note: "For ever" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or most early witnesses; Weymouth follows the latter. It may come from Jude 13, where it still stands.

records.change: Omits the closing "Amen"
records.note: The "Amen" is in Sinaiticus and the Byzantine text but not in Vaticanus; Weymouth follows the shorter reading. It is a liturgical ending.

records.change: "Jesus Christ his Son" becomes "Jesus, His Son"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or most early witnesses; Weymouth follows the latter. The cleansing power of his blood is unchanged.

records.change: Omits "Christ is come in the flesh"
records.note: The words are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or most early witnesses; Weymouth follows the latter. They stand in verse 2, which the critical text keeps.

records.change: "only begotten Son" becomes "only Son"
records.note: A translation choice for the Greek monogenēs, which can mean "only begotten" or "one and only"; Weymouth renders it "only". The Sonship is still stated.

records.change: Omits the heavenly witnesses: "the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus, some Latin manuscripts and a few late Greek ones (none earlier than about the 14th century); Weymouth omits them, following the earlier Greek witnesses. The Trinity is still taught elsewhere, as in Matthew 28:19.

records.change: Omits "in earth"
records.note: "In earth" belongs with the heavenly witnesses of verse 7 and has the same textual history; the three witnesses, the Spirit, water and blood, remain.

records.change: Omits "and that ye may believe on the name"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; Weymouth follows the latter. He also renders "eternal life" as "the Life of the Ages".

records.change: "keepeth himself" becomes "He who is God's Child keeps him"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads heauton ("himself"); Vaticanus and others read auton ("him"), which Weymouth follows and takes of Christ. Either way the believer is kept from the evil one.

records.change: Omits the closing "Amen"
records.note: The "Amen" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or most early witnesses; Weymouth follows the latter. It is a liturgical ending.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Jesus Christ"
records.note: "The Lord" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or most early witnesses; Weymouth follows the latter. He is still called the Son of the Father.

records.change: "transgresseth" becomes "presses on in advance"; second "of Christ" dropped
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads parabainōn ("transgresses"); Sinaiticus and Vaticanus read proagōn ("goes ahead"), which Weymouth follows. The warning against leaving Christ's teaching is unchanged.

records.change: Omits the closing "Amen"
records.note: The "Amen" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or most early witnesses; Weymouth follows the latter. It is a liturgical ending.

records.change: "only Lord God, and our Lord" becomes "only Sovereign and Lord"
records.note: "God" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P72, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; Weymouth follows the latter. In the shorter text both titles name Jesus Christ.

records.change: "for ever" becomes "of age-long duration"
records.note: A translation choice for the Greek eis aiōna, "for ever"; Weymouth's "age-long" can read as limited rather than endless.

records.change: "having not the Spirit" becomes "wholly unspiritual"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek pneuma mē echontes can mean "not having the Spirit" or "devoid of spirit"; Weymouth takes the second. Verses 19-20 still contrast them with those who pray in the Holy Spirit.

records.change: Omits "wise"; adds "through Jesus Christ our Lord", "before all time"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "the only wise God"; Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and others lack "wise" and add the other phrases, which Weymouth follows.

records.change: "washed us from our sins" becomes "freed us"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads lousanti ("washed"); P18, Sinaiticus and others read lysanti ("loosed"), which Weymouth follows. Both say it was by his own blood.

records.change: Omits "the beginning and the ending"; "Lord" becomes "Lord God"
records.note: "The beginning and the ending" is in Sinaiticus as first written, a few other manuscripts and the Textus Receptus, but not in Alexandrinus or most manuscripts, which also read "Lord God"; Weymouth follows them. It still stands in Revelation 21:6 and 22:13.

records.change: Omits "Christ" twice
records.note: "Christ" is in the Textus Receptus and many later manuscripts but not in Sinaiticus or Alexandrinus; Weymouth follows the latter. The meaning is unchanged.

records.change: Omits "I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus and a few late manuscripts but not in the Greek manuscripts generally; Weymouth follows them. Christ still says "I am the First and the Last" in 1:17.

records.change: "hell" becomes "Hades"; omits "Amen"
records.note: The Greek is hadēs, the place of the dead, which the KJV renders "hell"; the "Amen" is in the Byzantine text but not in Sinaiticus or Alexandrinus.

records.change: Omits "four and twenty" and "him that liveth for ever and ever"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or most other manuscripts; Weymouth follows the latter. The elders still fall down and worship.

records.change: "Hell" becomes "Hades"
records.note: The Greek is hadēs, the place of the dead, which the KJV renders "hell"; Weymouth keeps the Greek word, as most modern versions do.

records.change: "an angel" becomes "a solitary eagle"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads angelou ("angel"); the Greek manuscripts generally read aetou ("eagle"), which Weymouth follows. The message of woe is unchanged.

records.change: "the God of the earth" becomes "the Lord of the earth"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "God"; the critical text reads "Lord", which Weymouth follows. The meaning is unchanged.

records.change: Omits "and art to come"
records.note: The phrase is in the Textus Receptus and a few late manuscripts but not in the Greek manuscripts generally; Weymouth follows them. The verse goes on to say he has begun to reign.

records.change: Omits "Christ" after "testimony of Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Textus Receptus and some later manuscripts but not in Sinaiticus or Alexandrinus; Weymouth follows the latter. The meaning is unchanged.

records.change: Omits "before the throne of God"
records.note: The phrase is in the Textus Receptus and a few later manuscripts but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or most others; Weymouth follows the latter. They are still called faultless.

records.change: Omits "O Lord"; "and shalt be" becomes "the holy One"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "O Lord... and shalt be"; the Greek manuscripts read "who art and wast, the Holy One", which Weymouth follows. God is still addressed as righteous.

records.change: Omits "of heaven" after "temple"
records.note: The phrase is in the Textus Receptus and many later manuscripts but not in Alexandrinus or other early witnesses; Weymouth follows the latter. The voice still comes from the throne.

records.change: Omits "the Lord" and "honour"
records.note: Both words are in the Textus Receptus and some later manuscripts but not in Sinaiticus or Alexandrinus; Weymouth follows the latter. Salvation and glory are still ascribed to our God.

records.change: "the supper of the great God" becomes "God's great supper"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "the supper of the great God"; the critical text reads "the great supper of God", which Weymouth follows. The meaning is unchanged.

records.change: "stand before God" becomes "standing in front of the throne"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "God"; the critical text reads "the throne", which Weymouth follows. The meaning is unchanged.

records.change: "hell" becomes "Hades"
records.note: The Greek is hadēs, the place of the dead, which the KJV renders "hell"; Weymouth keeps the Greek word, as most modern versions do.

records.change: "hell" becomes "Hades"; adds "the Lake of fire"
records.note: "Hades" renders the Greek hadēs, the place of the dead. The closing "the lake of fire" is in Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus but not in the Textus Receptus; Weymouth follows the former.

records.change: Voice "out of heaven" becomes "from the throne"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "out of heaven"; Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus read "from the throne", which Weymouth follows. The message is unchanged.

records.change: Omits "God" as the one who wipes tears
records.note: "God" is in the Textus Receptus and many later manuscripts but not in Sinaiticus or Alexandrinus; Weymouth follows the latter. God is plainly the subject, from verse 3.

records.change: "do his commandments" becomes "wash their robes"
records.note: The Textus Receptus and the Byzantine text read "do his commandments"; Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus read "wash their robes", which Weymouth follows. Washing robes in the Lamb's blood is named in 7:14.

records.change: "the book of life" becomes "the Tree of Life"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "book"; every Greek manuscript reads "tree", which Weymouth follows. Erasmus took "book" from the Latin when the last verses of his Greek manuscript were missing.

records.change: Omits "our", "Christ" and "Amen"; "you all" becomes "God's people"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen"; the critical text reads "the Lord Jesus be with the saints" or "with all", which Weymouth follows. The blessing is unchanged.
